title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 14

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the planning meeting take place?
tasks.audioText: The student council is collecting ideas for a volunteering week in April. A planning meeting will take place in the student common room on Tuesday at twelve. Suggested activities include helping at a community garden, supporting a book collection and organising a repair café. Students should send one idea with a short explanation before the meeting.
options: On Tuesday at twelve
On Monday at twelve
On Tuesday at one
On Wednesday at twelve

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. What should students send before the meeting?
tasks.audioText: The student council is collecting ideas for a volunteering week in April. A planning meeting will take place in the student common room on Tuesday at twelve. Suggested activities include helping at a community garden, supporting a book collection and organising a repair café. Students should send one idea with a short explanation before the meeting.
options: A one-page proposal and short evidence summary
A list of suggested volunteering activities
A copy of the student council timetable
A completed attendance form

tasks.prompt: A group of students organised a repair café where local residents could bring small household items. Volunteers helped visitors identify simple problems and find repair information. The students did not attempt repairs that required specialist equipment or training. Instead, they explained where professional help was available. The event attracted many visitors and encouraged people to consider repairing items before replacing them. Reading 1. What did volunteers do when a repair needed specialist skills?
options: They repaired every item themselves
They asked visitors to buy replacement products
They explained where professional help was available
They directed visitors to the nearest supermarket

tasks.prompt: What wider effect did the event aim to encourage?
options: Encouraging residents to buy new household items
Encouraging people to repair items before replacing them
Encouraging visitors to donate electrical equipment
Encouraging residents to learn how to repair cars

tasks.prompt: The event was successful because local residents ___ to take part.
options: were invited
invited yesterday
are invite
have inviting

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO principles for a responsible volunteering activity.
options: Promise services that cannot be provided
Ignore safety requirements
Respect the needs of the community
Work within the volunteers' skills and training

tasks.prompt: A person who offers time to help others without payment is a ___.
A visitor asks you to repair an electrical item, but you are not trained. What should you say?
options: I can try anything, even without training.
I am not qualified to repair this, but I can help you find a suitable service.
Leave it with me and do not ask questions.
I will open it while it is connected.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of social responsibility in a logical order.
options: Organise people and safe resources
Find out what the community needs
Collect feedback and evaluate the result
Plan an activity within the team's abilities
correctOrder: Find out what the community needs
Plan an activity within the team's abilities
Collect feedback and evaluate the result

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words proposing a volunteering activity for students. Explain who it would help and how you would keep it safe and useful.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the proposed volunteering activity and the people it would help are identified (0–2); practical safety arrangements and how the activity would remain useful are explained (0–2); the plan is clearly organised with understandable grammar (0–2); volunteering/community/safety vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
